recipe_version.title: Senegalese Fish Yassa with Lemon-Mustard Onions and Rice
recipe_version.description: Broiled tilapia fillets under a heap of onions slowly cooked down in a lemon, Dijon, and garlic marinade until soft, golden, and jammy, with a whole habanero for gentle heat. Served over white rice with parsley and lemon.

ingredients.name: habanero chile
ingredients.note: removed before serving; gives gentle heat
ingredients.preparation: pierced twice with a knife, left whole

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp marinade, 1 tsp onions, 1/2 tsp rice

steps.title: Marinate and slice
steps.body: Juice 3 lemons (about 1/2 cup) and cut the fourth into wedges. In a large bowl whisk the lemon juice, Dijon, garlic, 1 tsp salt, and the pepper. Put the fish in a shallow dish, spoon 3 tbsp of the marinade over it, turn to coat, and refrigerate. Thinly slice the onions and toss them in the remaining marinade. Rinse the rice and chop the parsley.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.body: Combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp salt in a 2-quart saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, cover, reduce to low, and cook 15 minutes; then leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes. The covered cooking and rest run inside steps 3 and 4 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Cook down the onions
steps.body: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Lift the onions out of the marinade with tongs (keep the liquid) and cook, stirring every minute or two, until soft and browned at the edges, about 10 minutes. Add the reserved marinade, 1/2 cup water, the bay leaves, the habanero, and 1 tsp salt. Simmer over medium-low, partly covered and stirring every few minutes, until the onions are jammy and the sauce is thick and glossy, about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Broil the fish
steps.body: When the onions have about 12 minutes left, set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler and turn the broiler to high; let it heat 5 minutes. Brush a foil-lined sheet pan with 1 tbsp oil, lay the fillets on it, and broil 6 to 7 minutes, without turning, until opaque, flaking, 145 F in the center, and lightly browned at the edges. This runs inside the last 12 minutes of step 3 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Remove the bay leaves and habanero. Fluff the rice and divide it among plates. Set a fillet on each, heap the onions and their sauce over the fish, and finish with parsley and a lemon wedge.
